title: Fifteen nonnegative baseline slopes fall below independent-input bounds in 224 selected Allen electrical records
abstract: We tested a passive two-cell model against Allen mouse inhibitory electrical coupling summaries. Both pulse gains fixed the allowed baseline slope interval for independent zero-mean inputs or a nonnegative input cross-moment. Among 224 directed records from 112 pairs, 74 baseline slopes fell below the lower bound. Fifteen were nonnegative and therefore not failures of the usual zero-to-one voltage range. Six nonnegative cases remained in 68 records with both pulse p values below 0.05. Twelve main cases and five strict cases remained under an assumed factor 1.10 pulse error and 0.01 absolute baseline error. We derived the minimum magnitude of a negative normalized input cross-moment needed by the fixed two-cell model. Numerical optimization and independent moment checks agreed. Most records fit independent input moments. Hidden inputs, unknown means, finite pulse windows, fit error and selected slices prevent an inference of biological input anticorrelation or a general rejection of passive circuits. Code, aggregate results, a figure and external regeneration steps are supplied. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Counts under a conditional passive two-cell model and the minimum negative normalized input cross-moment magnitude. Directed records are not independent animals.
